channel.title: Daily Tech Briefing
channel.description: The day's top tech story in plain English — what happened, why it matters, and what to watch next. From dtbrief.com.

item.title: Jensen Huang Is Out.
item.description: Nvidia’s co-founder resigned Thursday after admitting to affairs, one with a suspected Chinese spy. Now Congress wants him to testify, the stock has slid below four trillion dollars in value, and the AI boom’s central company has no permanent leader.

item.title: Nvidia’s Board Moves to Oust Jensen Huang.
item.description: The board met Wednesday night to decide the fate of the co-founder who built the world’s most valuable chipmaker — after two affairs, one with a suspected Chinese spy, and a stock slide that has erased about $600 billion in value.

item.title: Anthropic’s IPO Roadshow Opens at $70 to $78 a Share.
item.description: Anthropic is selling 825 million shares and could raise up to $90.4 billion in total — the biggest test yet of Wall Street’s faith in the AI boom, and the valuation is not as simple as the headline number.

item.title: Anthropic’s Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 Are 20% Cheaper — and Days From an IPO.
item.description: Anthropic’s most capable models yet arrive faster and cheaper, with a price cut aimed squarely at developers — days before the biggest AI IPO ever.

item.title: Nvidia’s Board Opened a Probe Into Its Own CEO. The Company Is Worth $4.5 Trillion.
item.description: Jensen Huang admitted an affair and pledged to cooperate with an independent investigation, days before Nvidia reports earnings and Congress asks him to explain himself.

item.title: The AI Trade Imploded on Thursday. Tech Stocks Lost $2 Trillion in a Day.
item.description: The Nasdaq fell into correction territory as investors digested the Democrats’ midterm sweep — and the fear that the AI data-center buildout is about to get a lot harder to build.

item.title: OpenAI and Meta Bought Coding-Agent Startups on the Same Day. The Race Is Now for the Tools, Not Just the Models.
item.description: OpenAI is acquiring Pierre, whose code-storage libraries already power Codex, while Meta is acquiring Conductor, which orchestrates teams of coding agents — two deals that show the AI labs competing over the developer toolchain.

item.title: AMD Posted a Record $13.4 Billion Quarter. AI Data Centers Are Now Two-Thirds of Its Business.
item.description: Data-center sales nearly doubled to $8.5 billion on AI demand, and AMD guided to $17 billion next quarter — a sign the AI infrastructure boom is still accelerating.

item.title: Apple Posted a Record $114.5 Billion Quarter. The New Boss Passed His First Test — Mostly.
item.description: In John Ternus's first earnings report as CEO, Apple beat expectations on revenue and profit — but China revenue and iPad sales missed, and the company cannot make enough of its new foldable iPhone Duo.

item.title: OpenAI Raised Just $11 Billion of Its $30 Billion Target. The Blank-Check Era Is Over.
item.description: The ChatGPT maker wanted $30 billion at a $1.4 trillion valuation. It got about $11 billion at $1.25 trillion — and now it is turning to family offices and wealthy individuals to close the gap.

item.title: DoorDash Is Buying Instacart for $17 Billion. Here’s What Changes for Your Deliveries.
item.description: The restaurant-delivery giant is paying $65 a share for the grocery-delivery leader — a deal that would put dinner and your weekly shop under one roof, if regulators let it through.

item.title: Google’s Gemini 4 Carbon Is Its Strongest Security Model Yet. Almost Nobody Can Use It.
item.description: Google’s new frontier model tops harder benchmarks for finding and fixing security flaws — but access is limited to selected defenders, and its introductory price doubles soon.

item.title: Google’s Genie 4 Builds Worlds You Can Walk Through. Here’s What That Actually Means.
item.description: Google’s new world model generates photorealistic places you can explore, change with a text prompt, and hear — and it can hold the illusion together for two full minutes.

item.title: Anthropic Is Filing to Go Public at Up to $2 Trillion. Here’s What That Actually Means.
item.description: The maker of Claude filed its IPO paperwork on Monday, aiming to list on the Nasdaq under the ticker ANT as soon as the week before Thanksgiving — with a valuation that would make it one of the biggest listings in history.

item.title: SpaceX Just Borrowed $40 Billion to Buy AI Chips. Here’s What That Actually Means.
item.description: Elon Musk says the company closed $40 billion in mostly callable debt to buy Nvidia graphics chips — and used the announcement to declare the credit window shut for everyone else.

item.title: OpenAI Is About to Be Worth $1.25 Trillion. Here’s What That Actually Means.
item.description: A funding round of nearly $30 billion, led by investors from the United Arab Emirates, would put the maker of ChatGPT in the same league as Apple and Microsoft — before it has ever turned a profit.
